summary: Embedding payload corrupted by proxy compression upgrade causing large candidate loss and streaming stalls
description: Issue summary: Starting ~2026-03-12 11:45 UTC DocSearch reported that their reranking endpoint returned dramatically fewer candidates and streaming rerank requests stalled. Impact: 90% candidate suppression for multi-document rerank flows and ~30s tail stalls on streaming connections. Environment: dedicated tenant on prod (us-east), pinned to redwood-embed-v3-fp16. Symptoms appeared immediately following a scheduled proxy sidecar upgrade.
impact: DocSearch search UX degraded — rerank returned empty or single-candidate responses for ~majority of requests. Several customer API clients experienced streaming connections that never completed and timed out. Business impact: customer-reported feature outage affecting search relevance for active users.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer tenant credentials to call /v1/rerank with embedding vectors produced by redwood-embed-v3-fp16
2) Observe returned candidate list length and streaming behavior (server-sent events / chunked responses),
3) Re-run while toggling proxy compression flag (gzip vs none) or hitting a proxy version prior to 2026-03-12 to compare results
4) Capture raw request/response bodies from the proxy access logs for analysis
logs: 2026-03-12T11:46:03Z proxy-01 INFO forwarded request id=abc123 content-encoding=gzip payload-size=12460
investigation_notes: Correlation: spike in rerank empty-set events aligned to proxy sidecar rollout at 2026-03-12 11:40 UTC (deploy tag proxy-v2.14.0).
Hypothesis A: proxy compression/encoding layer mutated binary embedding payload on-the-wire (zero-padding or truncation) — resulting in 'orientation flip' signatures in embed decoding heuristics.

Hypothesis B: new compression library toggled a short-circuit that changed chunk framing for streams, causing the embed deserializer to interpret payload as little-endian vs expected big-endian for some message frames.

Evidence: raw proxy-forwarded bodies show repeated 0x00 paddings and occasional 0xFF sequences near embedding vectors; decode error rate on embed-service rose from 0.03% to 12% in the 5 minutes after deploy.
Repro attempt: hitting an older proxy instance (proxy-v2.13.4) reproduced expected candidate counts; running with compression disabled restored normal behavior for the failing tenant.
Temporary mitigation: blocked rollout to remaining hosts and placed failing proxy daemonset on rollback schedule.

root_cause_summary: A proxy-side compression/stream framing change introduced during the proxy-v2.14.0 rollout altered binary framing for some large embedding payloads. The embed-service decoder relied on stable framing/endianness and detected malformed frames, which led the reranker to drop candidates or return empty results; streaming chunk boundaries also caused stalls.
resolution: Immediate: rolled proxy rollout back to v2.13.4 for affected us-east pools, which restored correct behavior. Permanent: merged a patch to proxy that encodes embed payloads as base64 when compression is enabled to guarantee safe transport of binary vectors across chunked streams. Added unit and e2e tests that simulate large vector frames and integrated a canary deployment for 24h before full rollout.
workaround: For customers on dedicated instances, we temporarily disabled proxy-side compression on their tenant pool. Alternatively, customers could toggle to an older proxy route by setting X-Proxy-Route header to 'legacy' until the fixed version is deployed.

5) Tests: add fuzz tests for streaming chunk boundaries in CI for embed transport (owner: QA).
